I killed god and yet ants on the highest difficulty are extremely stressful.

What a magical game.

This is my first EDF and I have to say, it's simply awesome in some aspects, but also very rough all around. I was quite hesitant about getting it at first because I thought that it might not be fun enough in single player, and that the multiplayer would be basically dead. I was wrong on both accounts. It is fun solo, and the multiplayer is not dead at all.

So, what's good about it:
-the scale of the maps and missions
-the impressive number of enemies and allies at once on the battlefield
-the fact that every enemy type presents a widely different challenge
-the very distinct four classes
-the very large quantity of, once again, very distinct weapons
-the satisfaction that comes from how insane the firepower of those weapons is and the mayhem that they produce both it solo and multiplayer thanks to the blasts and friendly fire
-the inherent chaos caused by the size of the enemies and of their carcasses. Having the carcasses block bullets and movements in this game is just genius
-the npc banter and squad management in general, when it works
-the campy story

Now the bad:
-the game's content is too diluted, you get like a single new enemy type per 3 hours of playing. I honestly think the game would be better with half, or maybe even two-thirds of the missions removed. It doesn't make much sense in the first place to have a game that long when one of its main appeals is how replayable it is. Fewer missions would mean more fun switching around classes, weapons and difficulties. If removing those missions could save some budget to improve the remaining ones, even better.
-every crate except for the health ones. I see some vehement defenders for those but I honestly don't get it. It's just boring to have to run around collecting crates after the battle. Thankfully there are cheats that you can get online to make that aspect of the game disappear, but they all come with their own problems and limitations.
-it's kind of an extension of the game being too diluted, but the start of the game is extremely slow and boring. So boring in fact that I first gave up on the game after a few hours before coming back to it years later. It's terrible.
-the pricing is insane, especially for a multiplayer game. How do the developers expect me to be able to convince my friends to buy a game that is visibly ugly, janky and overall low-effort, when it costs 50€ per player? 200€ for a full team! Nearly five years after release! And there are 20 DLCs! Insane. Halve the price. Or give a free key to gift to a friend for every key bought. I really think they're just losing revenue and potential fans because of their pricing.
-the npc allies path-finding is horrendous, you'll very often have to go pick them up because they can't think of going around a wall or something
